title: After Completing My Study Abroad at the Medical University of Gdansk
paragraphs: For three months, from April to June 2006, I had the opportunity to do a clinical study abroad in Gdansk, a historic port city in northern Poland. The Medical University of Gdansk has an English department and participates in a European exchange program, so it is possible to receive medical education in English. It was also a reassuring encouragement that Professor Emeritus 若林隆 of Nagoya University was conducting research there as a professor. I did clerkships in cardiac surgery, palliative care, infectious diseases, neurology, urology, pediatrics and cardiology. Although the country is not economically wealthy, medical care is provided to European standards. The patients speak Polish and the charts are written in Polish, so it was not like a clerkship in an English-speaking country. However, I feel that the experience in Europe, where I came into contact with diverse values different from those in Japan, broadened the range of my own life experience and gave me a perspective for looking at things from many angles. In my free time, it was also meaningful to interact with exchange students from all over Europe and to be able to visit Krakow, Auschwitz and Germany on weekends. Europe, where different peoples and nations exist on a single continent separated by borders, is a completely different place from Japan, and its values are different too. Nowadays any information can be obtained on the Internet, but I realized that knowledge and experience are entirely different things. I would like my juniors, too, to experience things that can only be done while one is young.
